key_insight: Quantum feature selection performed similarly to random forest, showing that quantum methods can identify a small, useful feature set without sacrificing predictive performance.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical machine learning, QFS may help build compact, stable models from electronic health record data, potentially supporting more efficient clinical prediction workflows.
method: Compared two quantum feature selection approaches: quantum binary quadratic model (BQM) and constrained quadratic model (CQM).
Benchmarked them against random forest feature selection.
Used selected features to train an XGBoost classifier for urinary tract infection prediction.
evidence_signal: On 211 EHR-derived features, selecting 10 features gave median F1 scores of 0.60 (BQM), 0.61 (CQM), and 0.61 (random forest), with BQM and RF showing high stability.
watch_item: Results come from a single real-world task and depend on current quantum hardware and optimization setup, so broader generalization and practical deployment remain uncertain.
paper_title: Feature Selection with Quantum Annealing for Biomedical Machine Learning Applications
